briefdescription.para: Marmot's own vector-mode forward automatic differentiation with expression templates.

detaileddescription.para: VectorMode::Dual< nDirections > carries a value and its partial derivatives with respect to nDirections independent variables, so that one evaluation of a function yields a full Jacobian row. It is tailored to the first-derivative drivers df_dT, dF_dT and dF_dX< n > (and hence the tangents of the AD materials), where nDirections is small and known at compile time (6 or 9):

listitem.para: Arithmetic does not compute derivative arrays for intermediate results. It returns lightweight expression nodes, and the derivatives are computed in a single loop over the directions when an expression is assigned to a Dual.

Values are evaluated eagerly: when a node is created, it computes its value and the local partial derivatives with respect to its operands once. The loop over the directions then only combines the operands' derivatives linearly, i.e., elementary functions such as sqrt, exp, log or pow are never re-evaluated per direction.
Assignments may refer to the assigned number, e.g. x = x * y + z.
The partial derivatives are stored before the value, so that pairs of them are 16-byte aligned for SIMD.

detaileddescription.para: Expression nodes keep their sub-expressions by value, but refer to the Dual numbers they are built from. An expression must therefore not outlive its full-expression: never store one in auto, and never return one from a function or lambda with a deduced return type. Name the number type (Dual, or JacobianDual) instead.
Use this header through the backend-neutral vocabulary of MarmotAutomaticDifferentiationTypes.h (JacobianDual, value, seedDirection, partialDerivative).

codeline.highlight: Comparable=(Expression< A >&&(Expression< B >||Constant< B >))||(Constant< A >&&Expression< B >);
